newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania commercial bank loses licence.
newsitem.headline: Romania commercial bank loses licence.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) stripped a third commercial bank of its licence after more than a year of failing to perform banking operations, a BNR decision printed in the country's official gazette showed on Friday.
Euro Express Bank had conducted no operations since acquiring a licence on April 12, 1996, the decision said.
A Euro Expres Bank official said the BNR had notified Euro Express of its decision.
"The ruling was correct and in line with BNR rules, which say that a bank loses its licence if it fails to operate for 12 months after creation," the official said.
Last month, the central bank withdrew licences from troubled private banks Dacia Felix and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank, saying they had big debts and low capitalisation.
That move is subject to long court cases to determine whether the two banks should be reorganised or liquidated.
No local bank has been declared bankrupt since Romania ousted communists in 1989 and restructured its banking system. Around 40 commercial banks are now in operation.
